category_title: Honors students experiencing anxiety with higher-order analytical tasks
scenario_title: Transitioning from theoretical reading to actual qualitative data analysis
minimal_context: The student is transitioning from reading about qualitative methods to coding and analyzing their collected field notes for their honors project.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Now that the research deadlines are nearing, it is time to move from the assigned readings to actually coding and analyzing your field notes.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I was really optimistic about my abilities to successfully engage in the research process early on. But now that we actually have to do it, I'm starting to question my abilities, despite the fact that I have previously taken another research methods class.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try to process the information and find patterns in your data.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It is much easier to regurgitate information than to process it, try to find patterns, make sense of it, and see it applied in the larger picture. I'm surprised at my feelings of frustration and inadequacy given the relative ease I've experienced in my other honors courses.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Go ahead and start coding the data you collected.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm absolutely petrified. Talking and reading about versus doing qualitative research is the same as if I read a book on 'the process of how to successfully catch an Amazon Marmoset', and then someone tossed me into the rain forest expecting me to find my way. My anticipation has melted into fear and doubt, and I can not help but think I am way out of my league.

task.content: Progressing through the research steps of the honors qualitative methods project, including data collection, analysis, and interpretation; specifically coding, analyzing data, interviewing, and observing.
task.learning_goal: To process information, try to find patterns, make sense of it, and see it applied in the larger picture.

context.environment: Upper-division qualitative research methods honors seminar, including a cafeteria area for observation.
context.materials: Weekly journals, field notes, assigned readings.
context.social_setting: Research team of peers, class discussions, and private dialogue with the instructor.
context.time_context: As research deadlines neared and students actually began to engage in research.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: As research deadlines neared and students actually began to engage in research, moving from reading about the process to doing it.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Questioned her abilities despite the fact that she had previously taken another research methods class; described her experience in the course in terms of a child's perception of an amusement park.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Significant anxiety about their abilities to accomplish research tasks; anticipation melted into fear and doubt; absolutely petrified.
related_quotes: Talking and reading about versus doing qualitative research is the same as if I read a book on ‘the process of how to successfully catch an Amazon Marmoset ’, and then someone tossed me into the rain forest expecting me to find my way, identify which freakin ’species of monkey is a marmoset, and then catch the little creature.

My moment had finally come. As I stood in front of the gargantuan wooden structure all I could hear was the screams of passengers ...my anticipation melted into fear and doubt. I was absolutely petrified. As I was strapped into the roller coaster seat I could not help but think it was too big for me, I was way out of my league.

behavior_patterns.condition: When faced with the cognitive work of analysis.
